question: The LaQshya programme launched by the Government of India primarily aims to improve which aspect of maternal and newborn care?

answers.text: Antenatal screening for gestational diabetes in all trimesters

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Antenatal GDM screening is part of DIPSI and IADPSG protocols, not the specific focus of LaQshya. LaQshya targets the intrapartum and immediate postpartum period.

answers.text: Quality of care in labour rooms and maternity operation theatres through respectful, evidence-based intrapartum care

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. LaQshya (Labour Room Quality Improvement Initiative) was launched in 2017 to improve the quality and respectfulness of care in labour rooms and maternity operation theatres at public health facilities, aiming to reduce preventable maternal and newborn mortality and morbidity.

answers.text: Postpartum family planning counselling at six weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Postpartum family planning is an important maternal health goal but is addressed through programmes like RMNCH+A, not through LaQshya, which focuses on intrapartum care quality.

answers.text: Immunisation coverage for all newborns in the first 24 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Newborn immunisation (BCG, OPV, Hepatitis B at birth) falls under the Universal Immunisation Programme, not LaQshya.

overallFeedback.feedback: LaQshya is an intrapartum quality initiative targeting labour rooms and OTs at public hospitals. MuSQan complements it for postpartum and newborn care quality.
Well done. LaQshya = Labour room Quality (intrapartum + immediate postpartum). Its companion programme MuSQan focuses on postpartum and newborn care quality.
